calls.name: actors
calls.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: transparent game character sprite sheet.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and controls all character identities, palette, poses, order and placement. Image 2 is a STYLE REFERENCE for visible pixel size and simplified pixel clusters only; do not copy any of its characters, scenery, props, layout or UI.
Primary request: Redraw Image 1 as unmistakably COARSE LOW-RESOLUTION PIXEL ART. Change only the rendering and remove the existing background to true transparent alpha. Keep our original characters, their costume colors, poses and placement. The previous sprites have far too much painterly detail: substantially simplify them into bold square pixel clusters.
Composition: Exactly 3 columns x 4 rows, equally spaced cells; no lines or labels. Output portrait 2:3, ideally 1024x1536. Hero fills rows 1-2, facing RIGHT: row 1 idle, windup, strike; row 2 guard, hurt, death. Rival fills rows 3-4, facing LEFT: row 3 idle, windup, strike; row 4 guard, hurt, death. Preserve each exact pose from Image 1. Hero has cyan masked hood, navy/teal clothing, red scarf, curved sword and small round shield. Rival is an armored undead knight with dark armor, copper plates, green ragged cape and glowing green long-handled axe.
Pixel construction: Each upright body is approximately 48-64 logical pixels tall, shown with uniform hard 5-6-pixel square blocks as though enlarged with NEAREST NEIGHBOR. Make pixel steps extremely visible. Use only 16-24 solid colors per figure and 2-3 flat shades per material. Simplify anatomy, armor, folds, faces, scarf and weapons into strong readable silhouettes. Edges are stepped square blocks, internal shading is large solid clusters. Strike effects are a few simple stepped pixel shapes.
Constraints: Every figure and its complete weapon/effect stays entirely inside its own cell with generous transparent margins and clear empty gaps. No overlapping neighboring cells or clipped weapons. Upright feet share a consistent baseline within their row; death sprites lie low in their cells. Output genuine alpha transparency around all sprites, no painted background, no checkerboard baked into image, no ground or shadow plane. No text, borders, labels or UI.
Avoid: fine texture, engraving, noise, tiny scattered detail, stippling, detailed anatomy, smooth outlines, vector curves, anti-aliasing, blur, painterly brushwork, realistic volume, gradients on bodies. Do not merely overlay a pixel filter onto detailed art; actually rebuild it from coarse limited-color pixel clusters. Do not import or copy proprietary Dead Cells sprites.

calls.name: icons
calls.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: transparent game inventory icon sheet.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, controlling icon identities, colors, silhouettes, order and placement. Image 2 is a STYLE REFERENCE only for coarse pixel size and simplified pixel clusters. Do not copy its proprietary icons, characters, scenery or UI.
Primary request: Redraw all twelve original icons of Image 1 as very coarse, crisp low-resolution pixel art. Change only the rendering. Preserve each icon's recognizable identity, palette and placement while radically simplifying tiny details.
Composition: Exactly 4 columns x 3 rows, regular equal cells, isolated icons centered with generous transparent margins. Preserve order: row 1 curved blade, round shield, purple lightning crystal (spark), golden sun/compass medallion (focus); row 2 green venom bottle, round fuse bomb, red heart, gold skull coin; row 3 amber potion flask, cyan ghost-in-bottle relic, copper crown with red jewel, cyan four-point star. Output landscape approximately 4:3, ideally 1536x1152. No grid lines or labels.
Pixel construction: Each icon is only 24-32 logical pixels across its major dimension, enlarged 8-10 times with nearest-neighbor appearance. Pixel blocks must be plainly visible and uniformly square. Use just 8-16 solid colors per icon, thick blocky outlines and 2-3 flat shades per material, strong simple shapes. Preserve only big defining features. Simplify the heart, coin skull, bottle, crown and magic effects into minimal readable symbols rather than illustrations. A few chunky clusters suffice for highlights and energy.
Constraints: Genuine transparent alpha background around each icon; no baked checkerboard, no black backdrop, no panels. Complete icons and effects contained inside their own cells, clear gaps, no overlapping, no cropping. No text, numbers, borders or UI. Preserve all twelve identities and their order.
Avoid: fine edging, fine textures, engraving, tiny noise, complicated bevels, painterly shading, smooth curves, blur, anti-aliasing, realistic volume or anatomy, gradients, detailed miniature illustration. Rebuild using coarse limited-color pixel clusters instead of applying a pixel filter to detailed art.

calls.name: arena
calls.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: empty side-view game arena background.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and controls original scenery, composition, platform height, architecture and palette. Image 2 is a STYLE REFERENCE for visible pixel size, broad pixel clusters and simplified forms only. Do not copy Image 2's actual scenery, moon, bridge design, characters, props or UI.
Primary request: Redraw our original ruined seaside castle arena from Image 1 as visibly coarse low-resolution pixel art, substantially simplifying the overly detailed painterly rendering. Keep the original composition and scene identity.
Scene/composition: Empty side view of a ruined stone bridge/platform between dark ruined castle walls at left and right, distant central gothic island castle beyond teal sea, cyan sky and purple-red sunset clouds, a few warm torches and hanging cages as in Image 1. Keep the broad open center, original foreground wall framing, sea horizon and distant castle position. Keep the flat playable stone platform at precisely the same normalized height as Image 1, about 78 percent down the canvas, with the stone platform structure continuing to the bottom. Output 16:9 landscape, ideally 1600x900.
Pixel construction: Construct the whole image as though painted on a roughly 320x180 logical-pixel canvas and enlarged with nearest-neighbor. Hard square steps and large solid-color clusters must be immediately visible on every physical form. Use chunky stone blocks, broad cloud masses, simplified tower silhouettes and sparse large highlights. Restrict the scenery to a compact palette of teal, navy, purple, cyan and red/coral sunset tones with restrained warm torch accents. Preserve atmospheric depth with simple broad shapes and value layers. Broad atmospheric glow may remain, but architecture, stones, sea reflections, plants and clouds must be unmistakably coarse pixel forms.
Constraints: Keep our own original scenery and placement. No people, monsters, items, text, numbers, logos, labels, UI, health bars or borders. Full opaque background.
Avoid: dense tiny texture, photorealism, fine brickwork, micro-detail, noise, stippling, smooth physical contours, delicate foliage, painterly brushwork, detailed rendering under a pixel filter. Do not import or recreate proprietary Dead Cells scenery.
